First off, you don't know that. In fact Bitcoin is a medium that is often employed for international trade, especially in regions with stifling regulation and/or animosity towards foreigners. As such it's exceptionally well made to accomodate "gray trades."

This achieves three ends: First of all, it avoids state intervention and taxation, second it avoids bank intervention and fees, third it still achieves documentable trades, which are highly valuable to any business venture, big and small. In a general sense, Bitcoin is exceptionally good at avoiding middlemen.

Only Good for Small Transactions

​Otherwise you're right in that small transactions of gold are free, because they require no proof of work. However you already paid the markup for the mining.

Whenever you need to ship a large amount of gold, you're in a heap of trouble, though. For instance, how can you guarantee safety during the shipping? And how can you guarantee that it won't be impounded or delayed by state officials? And how do you fend off would-be robbers? These are all very real concerns when dealing with a big shipment of gold.

The fact is that gold is a horrible asset to use for world trade unless you employ certificates, and even then you're subject to rampant overprinting of such certificates, and not least the various and spurious bank and state regulations, taxations and fees. In other words, using gold exposes you to heaps of greedy middlemen, if you're not straigth up mugged.

Documentation is an Asset

On the other hand, Bitcoin's transactions aren't free, because they can also be used to document transactions, so you can prove in court that you made a legal purchase with it. You can even send a short signed message with it, proving what the transaction was for. This is in fact a very useful attribute of Bitcoin.

Not so with gold. If you give it away, you better get something for it that is materal and that you can hold in your hand. A receipt is something, but only if you are able to safely keep it. As such, gold can certainly be good as a medium of last resort, but if you're already in such a bind, then chances are that it can be taken from you by force, and there would be nothing to prove it.

International Trade

As such, Bitcoin is a far better medium to make big purchases, for instance with things such as realestate, or factory equipment, or big shipments of minerals or oil, and so on. It's great for anything that requires some assurance or guarantee. Again that shows why Bitcoin is far more useful in big business than gold.

Further more, if you cross a border, it can't be impounded by the toll guards. If you travel, it's extremely unlikely that it can be taken by muggers or highway robbers. Not so with gold. It is easily impounded or stolen, and if you're not given a receipt, there would be no proof of it either, so good luck complaining about it.

Gold Best for Black Economies

Now, of course, sometimes that's a trait you want, if you delve into black economics, but usually not. And so gold is relegated to speculation on receipts, fancy jewlery, or highly underpriced electronic equipment made largely by Asian factory slaves.

So while gold is subject to heaps and heaps of greedy middlemen, the only guys being paid for Bitcoin, are the ones actually working for it, and only as much as you're willing to pay for it in order for your transaction to be finalized sooner.
